verses.text: Listen, heavens, and I will speak. Hear, earth, the words from my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain, and my words come down like dew, like gentle rain on new grass, like showers on young plants.
I will announce the name of the LORD. Praise the greatness of our God!
He is the Rock, and his work is perfect. Everything he does is just. He is a faithful God who does no wrong. He is fair and right.
But they have acted wickedly toward him. Because of their sin they are no longer his children. They are a twisted and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish and senseless people? Is he not your Father, who made you his own? He created you and formed you.
Remember the days of long ago. Think about the generations of the past. Ask your father, and he will tell you. Ask your elders, and they will explain it to you.
When the Most High gave the nations their lands, when he divided up the human race, he set the borders of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
For the LORD's own share is his people. Jacob is the part he chose for himself.
He found him in a desert land, in an empty land of howling winds. He surrounded him and cared for him. He protected him like the pupil of his own eye.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, he spread out his wings to catch them and carried them on his feathers.
The LORD alone led him. No foreign god was with him.
He let him ride over the high places of the land and eat the crops of the fields. He fed him with honey from the rock and olive oil from the hard stone,
with butter from the herd and milk from the flock, with the fat of lambs and goats, with fine rams from Bashan, and with the best wheat. You drank wine made from the juice of grapes.
Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, heavy, and full of food. Then he abandoned the God who made him and rejected the Rock who saved him.
They made him jealous with foreign gods and angered him with their hateful idols.
They sacrificed to demons, which are not God, to gods they had not known, new gods that had only just appeared, gods your ancestors did not fear.
You forgot the Rock who became your father. You forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw this and rejected them, because his sons and daughters had made him angry.
He said, "I will hide my face from them and see what happens to them in the end. For they are a twisted generation, children who cannot be trusted.

They made me jealous with something that is not a god and angered me with their worthless idols. So I will make them jealous with people who are not a nation. I will make them angry with a nation that has no understanding.
For my anger has started a fire that burns down to the deepest grave. It will burn up the earth and its crops and set fire to the foundations of the mountains.
I will pile disasters on them and use up all my arrows against them.
They will waste away from hunger and be eaten up by burning fever and deadly disease. I will send wild animals with their teeth against them, and poisonous snakes that crawl in the dust.
Outside, the sword will kill their children. Inside their homes, terror will strike. Young men and young women will die, babies and old men with grey hair.
I said I would scatter them far away and wipe out all memory of them from the earth.
But I was afraid of what their enemies would say. Their enemies might misunderstand and say, 'We won by our own power. It was not the LORD who did all this.'"
Israel is a nation without sense. There is no understanding in them.
If only they were wise and understood this! If only they would think about what will happen to them in the end!
How could one enemy chase a thousand of them, or two enemies make ten thousand run away, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had given them up?
For their rock is not like our Rock. Even our enemies agree with that.
Their vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are full of poison, and their bunches are bitter.
Their wine is like the poison of snakes, the deadly venom of cobras.
"Have I not kept this in store, sealed up in my treasure rooms?
It is mine to pay back and to punish. In due time their feet will slip. Their day of disaster is near, and their ruin is rushing toward them."
The LORD will do justice for his people and have mercy on his servants, when he sees that their strength is gone and no one is left, neither slave nor free.
He will say, "Now where are their gods, the rock they ran to for safety,
the gods who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let those gods get up and help you! Let them protect you!
See now that I, I alone, am he. There is no other god beside me. I put to death and I bring to life. I wound and I heal. No one can rescue anyone from my hand.
I lift my hand to heaven and make this promise: As surely as I live forever,
when I sharpen my flashing sword and take hold of it to judge, I will pay back my enemies and punish those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will eat flesh: the blood of the killed and the captured, the heads of the enemy leaders."
Celebrate with his people, you nations, for he will pay back those who killed his servants. He will punish his enemies and make his land and his people clean again.
Moses came with Joshua son of Nun and recited all the words of this song so the people could hear.
When Moses had finished reciting all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I have solemnly declared to you today. Command your children to carefully obey all the words of this law.
These are not just empty words for you. They are your life. By obeying them you will live a long time in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take over."
That same day the LORD said to Moses,
"Go up into the Abarim Mountains to Mount Nebo in Moab, across from Jericho. Look out over Canaan, the land I am giving the Israelites as their own.
There on the mountain you have climbed you will die and join your people who have died before you, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and joined his people.
For both of you were unfaithful to me in front of the Israelites at the waters of Meribah Kadesh in the Desert of Zin. You did not show my holiness among the Israelites.
So you will see the land only from a distance. You will not enter the land I am giving the Israelites."
